section_1.title: The Big Picture: Learning as Fine-Tuning
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a neural network as a series of adjustable 'dials' (weights). Explain that 'learning' is simply the process of turning these dials to get the correct output for a given input. Establish the prerequisite: inputs are numbers, and weights are multipliers.
section_1.example: Imagine a Robot Chef trying to bake the perfect cookie. The 'inputs' are flour and sugar amounts; the 'dials' are how long it bakes and at what temperature.

section_2.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
section_2.content: Demonstrate the flow of information. Explain how inputs are multiplied by weights and passed through an activation function (the 'gatekeeper') to produce a final prediction. Use a graphical flow from left to right.
section_2.example: The Robot Chef sets the oven to 350°F (Weight A) for 10 minutes (Weight B). The result? A cookie that is slightly burnt (The Output).

section_3.title: The Loss Function: Measuring the Mistake
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Cost' or 'Loss' function. Explain that to improve, we must mathematically calculate exactly how far off the prediction was from the truth. Visualize this as a 'Distance' on a graph.
section_3.example: We compare the burnt cookie to a 'Perfect Cookie' template. The difference in darkness and texture is our 'Error Score'.

section_4.title: Backpropagation: The Blame Game
section_4.content: This is the core concept. Work backward from the error to see which 'dial' (weight) contributed most to the mistake. Explain that backpropagation is the application of the 'Chain Rule'—calculating the sensitivity of the final error to each individual weight.
section_4.example: We look at the burnt cookie and ask: 'Was it mostly the temperature dial or the timer dial that caused this?' If the timer was off by 5 minutes but the temp only by 2 degrees, the timer gets more 'blame'.

section_5.title: Gradient Descent: Walking Down the Hill
section_5.content: Introduce the visual of a 'Loss Landscape' (a hilly terrain). Explain that the 'Gradient' tells us the direction of the steepest uphill. To learn, we take a small step in the opposite direction (downhill) to minimize error.
section_5.example: The Robot Chef is in a foggy valley. It feels the slope under its feet and takes one small step toward the lowest point (the recipe with the least error).

section_6.title: The Iteration: Practice Makes Perfect
section_6.content: Summarize that one step isn't enough. Learning is a cycle: Forward pass, calculate error, backpropagate blame, update dials, and repeat thousands of times until the error is near zero.
section_6.example: The Robot Chef bakes 1,000 batches. Each time, it nudges the dials slightly based on the previous error, eventually discovering the 'Golden Recipe'.

section_4.content: This is the core concept. Work backward from the error to see which 'dial' (weight) contributed most to the mistake. Explain that backpropagation is the application of the 'Chain Rule'—calculating the sensitivity of the final error to each individual weight.
section_4.example: We look at the burnt cookie and ask: 'Was it mostly the temperature dial or the timer dial that caused this?' If the timer was off by 5 minutes but the temp only by 2 degrees, the timer gets more 'blame'.

section_5.title: Gradient Descent: Walking Down the Hill
section_5.content: Introduce the visual of a 'Loss Landscape' (a hilly terrain). Explain that the 'Gradient' tells us the direction of the steepest uphill. To learn, we take a small step in the opposite direction (downhill) to minimize error.
section_5.example: The Robot Chef is in a foggy valley. It feels the slope under its feet and takes one small step toward the lowest point (the recipe with the least error).

section_6.title: The Iteration: Practice Makes Perfect
section_6.content: Summarize that one step isn't enough. Learning is a cycle: Forward pass, calculate error, backpropagate blame, update dials, and repeat thousands of times until the error is near zero.
section_6.example: The Robot Chef bakes 1,000 batches. Each time, it nudges the dials slightly based on the previous error, eventually discovering the 'Golden Recipe'.

lecture_lines: Inputs enter the network and travel from left to right.

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.place_in_area(weights_label, "B3", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)

        sugar_label = Text("Sugar", font_size=16, color="#FFD700")

        flour_icon = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.4, color="#FFD700"), flour_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        sugar_icon = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.4, color="#FFD700"), sugar_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(flour_icon, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(sugar_icon, "D1")
        
        # Dial icon
        dial_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00FF00")
        dial_pointer = Line(dial_circle.get_center(), dial_circle.get_top(), color="#00FF00")

        self.place_at_grid(dial, "C4")

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Burnt Cookie at output
        burnt_label = Text("Burnt", font_size=16, color="#8B4513")
        burnt_cookie = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.3, color="#8B4513", fill_opacity=0.8), burnt_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(burnt_cookie, "C6")
        
        # Perfect Cookie
        perfect_label = Text("Perfect", font_size=16, color="#F5DEB3")
        perfect_cookie = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.3, color="#F5DEB3", fill_opacity=0.8), perfect_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(perfect_cookie, "C6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(burnt_cookie))
        
        # Rotate dial and scale weights
        self.play(
            Rotate(dial, angle=PI/2),
            weights_label.animate.scale(1.2),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Transform cookie
        self.play(Transform(burnt_cookie, perfect_cookie))
        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        )

            ReplacementTransform(uphill_arrow, downhill_arrow),

        self.play(
            dot.animate.move_to(step_pos),
            FadeOut(downhill_arrow),
            FadeOut(step_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Iteratively move to the bottom
        bottom_pos = curve_center + np.array([0, 0, 0])
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(bottom_pos), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Walking downhill reduces the overall cost of our model.
        # Fade in the text 'Minimum Error' in #00FF00 at the lowest point of the curve.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        min_error_text = Text("Minimum Error", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        min_error_text.next_to(dot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(min_error_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Big Picture: Learning as Fine-Tuning
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a neural network as a series of adjustable 'dials' (weights). Explain that 'learning' is simply the process of turning these dials to get the correct output for a given input. Establish the prerequisite: inputs are numbers, and weights are multipliers.
section_1.example: Imagine a Robot Chef trying to bake the perfect cookie. The 'inputs' are flour and sugar amounts; the 'dials' are how long it bakes and at what temperature.

section_2.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
section_2.content: Demonstrate the flow of information. Explain how inputs are multiplied by weights and passed through an activation function (the 'gatekeeper') to produce a final prediction. Use a graphical flow from left to right.
section_2.example: The Robot Chef sets the oven to 350°F (Weight A) for 10 minutes (Weight B). The result? A cookie that is slightly burnt (The Output).

section_3.title: The Loss Function: Measuring the Mistake
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Cost' or 'Loss' function. Explain that to improve, we must mathematically calculate exactly how far off the prediction was from the truth. Visualize this as a 'Distance' on a graph.
section_3.example: We compare the burnt cookie to a 'Perfect Cookie' template. The difference in darkness and texture is our 'Error Score'.

section_4.title: Backpropagation: The Blame Game
section_4.content: This is the core concept. Work backward from the error to see which 'dial' (weight) contributed most to the mistake. Explain that backpropagation is the application of the 'Chain Rule'—calculating the sensitivity of the final error to each individual weight.
section_4.example: We look at the burnt cookie and ask: 'Was it mostly the temperature dial or the timer dial that caused this?' If the timer was off by 5 minutes but the temp only by 2 degrees, the timer gets more 'blame'.

section_5.title: Gradient Descent: Walking Down the Hill
section_5.content: Introduce the visual of a 'Loss Landscape' (a hilly terrain). Explain that the 'Gradient' tells us the direction of the steepest uphill. To learn, we take a small step in the opposite direction (downhill) to minimize error.
section_5.example: The Robot Chef is in a foggy valley. It feels the slope under its feet and takes one small step toward the lowest point (the recipe with the least error).

section_6.title: The Iteration: Practice Makes Perfect
section_6.content: Summarize that one step isn't enough. Learning is a cycle: Forward pass, calculate error, backpropagate blame, update dials, and repeat thousands of times until the error is near zero.
section_6.example: The Robot Chef bakes 1,000 batches. Each time, it nudges the dials slightly based on the previous error, eventually discovering the 'Golden Recipe'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Big Picture: Learning as Fine-Tuning"
        lines = [
            "Neural networks learn by adjusting internal parameters called weights.",
            "Think of weights as dials on a machine.",
            "Tuning these dials helps the network produce correct outputs."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Neural networks learn by adjusting internal parameters called weights.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Nodes
        input_node1 = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE)
        input_node2 = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE)
        output_node = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(input_node1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(input_node2, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(output_node, "C5")
        
        # Connections
        line1 = Line(input_node1.get_right(), output_node.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        line2 = Line(input_node2.get_right(), output_node.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        
        # Weights Label
        weights_label = Text("Weights", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(weights_label, "B3", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(input_node1), Create(input_node2), Create(output_node))
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.play(Write(weights_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Think of weights as dials on a machine.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        
        # Flour and Sugar icons entering
        flour_label = Text("Flour", font_size=16, color="#FFD700")
        sugar_label = Text("Sugar", font_size=16, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Using simple shapes for icons as no external assets provided
        flour_icon = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.4, color="#FFD700"), flour_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        sugar_icon = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.4, color="#FFD700"), sugar_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(flour_icon, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(sugar_icon, "D1")
        
        # Dial icon
        dial_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00FF00")
        dial_pointer = Line(dial_circle.get_center(), dial_circle.get_top(), color="#00FF00")
        dial = VGroup(dial_circle, dial_pointer)
        self.place_at_grid(dial, "C4")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(flour_icon, shift=RIGHT),
            FadeIn(sugar_icon, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        self.play(Create(dial))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Tuning these dials helps the network produce correct outputs.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Burnt Cookie at output
        burnt_label = Text("Burnt", font_size=16, color="#8B4513")
        burnt_cookie = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.3, color="#8B4513", fill_opacity=0.8), burnt_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(burnt_cookie, "C6")
        
        # Perfect Cookie
        perfect_label = Text("Perfect", font_size=16, color="#F5DEB3")
        perfect_cookie = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.3, color="#F5DEB3", fill_opacity=0.8), perfect_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(perfect_cookie, "C6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(burnt_cookie))
        
        # Rotate dial and scale weights
        self.play(
            Rotate(dial, angle=PI/2),
            weights_label.animate.scale(1.2),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Transform cookie
        self.play(Transform(burnt_cookie, perfect_cookie))
        self.wait(2)

            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        self.play(Write(timer_grad), Write(temp_grad))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "This assigns \"blame\" to specific dials in the system."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The loss landscape is like a hilly, foggy terrain.",
            "The gradient points in the steepest uphill direction.",
            "We take a small step in the opposite direction.",
            "This process iteratively moves the network toward minimum error.",
            "Walking downhill reduces the overall cost of our model."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Gradient Descent: Walking Down the Hill", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a smooth U-shaped curve in #FFFFFF representing the 'Loss Landscape'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * (x**2), x_range=[-2.2, 2.2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        curve_center = curve.get_center()
        
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The gradient points in the steepest uphill direction.
        # Place a small 'Robot Chef' dot (#FFD700) at a high position on the slope.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        local_x_start = -1.6
        local_y_start = 0.5 * (local_x_start**2)
        dot = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.1)
        dot.move_to(curve_center + np.array([local_x_start, local_y_start, 0]))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        # Gradient arrow (uphill)
        uphill_arrow = Arrow(
            start=dot.get_center(), 
            end=dot.get_center() + np.array([-0.6, 0.9, 0]), 
            color="#00FF00", 
            buff=0
        )
        grad_label = Text("Gradient", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        grad_label.next_to(uphill_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(uphill_arrow), FadeIn(grad_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # We take a small step in the opposite direction.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Step arrow (downhill) - opposite of gradient
        downhill_arrow = Arrow(
            start=dot.get_center(), 
            end=dot.get_center() + np.array([0.6, -0.9, 0]), 
            color="#00FF00", 
            buff=0
        )
        step_label = Text("Step Down", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        step_label.next_to(downhill_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(uphill_arrow, downhill_arrow),
            ReplacementTransform(grad_label, step_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This process iteratively moves the network toward minimum error.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move dot one small 'step' down
        local_x_step = -0.8
        local_y_step = 0.5 * (local_x_step**2)
        step_pos = curve_center + np.array([local_x_step, local_y_step, 0])
        
        self.play(
            dot.animate.move_to(step_pos),
            FadeOut(downhill_arrow),
            FadeOut(step_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Iteratively move to the bottom
        bottom_pos = curve_center + np.array([0, 0, 0])
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(bottom_pos), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Walking downhill reduces the overall cost of our model.
        # Fade in the text 'Minimum Error' in #00FF00 at the lowest point of the curve.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        min_error_text = Text("Minimum Error", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        min_error_text.next_to(dot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(min_error_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Iteration: Practice Makes Perfect",
            [
                "Learning requires repeating this cycle thousands of times.",
                "Each pass nudges the weights closer to perfection.",
                "Practice eventually transforms a random guess into accuracy."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        color_cycle = "#00BFFF"
        color_highlight = "#FFD700"
        
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_cycle))

        # Create cycle components
        forward_text = Text("Forward", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        loss_text = Text("Loss", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        backprop_text = Text("Backprop", font_size=20, color=WHITE)

        self.place_at_grid(loss_text, "A5")
        self.place_in_area(backprop_text, "C3", "C4")

        # Simple center for rotation (approximate)
        center_pos = (self.grid["B3"] + self.grid["B4"]) / 2
        
        # Circular Arrow Representation
        circle_path = Circle(radius=1.5, color=color_cycle).move_to(center_pos)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cycle_group), Create(circle_path))
        self.play(Rotate(circle_path, angle=TAU, about_point=center_pos), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_highlight)

            y_range=[0, 1, 0.2],

        )

            lambda x: 0.8 * np.exp(-0.5 * x),
            color=color_highlight,
            x_range=[0, 10]
        )

        self.play(Create(error_curve), run_time=4)

        self.wait(2)

outline.content: Demonstrate the flow of information. Explain how inputs are multiplied by weights and passed through an activation function (the 'gatekeeper') to produce a final prediction. Use a graphical flow from left to right.
outline.example: The Robot Chef sets the oven to 350°F (Weight A) for 10 minutes (Weight B). The result? A cookie that is slightly burnt (The Output).

storyboard.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
lecture_lines: Inputs enter the network and travel from left to right.
Each input is multiplied by a weight.
Weighted values are summed at each neuron.
An activation function acts as a gatekeeper for signals.
The final output is the network's current prediction.
animations: Show input values like '350' and '10' in #ADD8E6 appearing on the left side of the screen.
Animate lines with labels 'x Weight' (#FF69B4) connecting these inputs to a central 'Gatekeeper' node.
Pulse the 'Gatekeeper' node in #FF4500 and reveal the 'Burnt Cookie' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cookie.svg] prediction value on the right.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "Inputs enter the network and travel from left to right.",
            "Each input is multiplied by a weight.",
            "Weighted values are summed at each neuron.",
            "An activation function acts as a gatekeeper for signals.",
            "The final output is the network's current prediction."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Forward Pass: Making a Guess", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard and prompt requirements
        input_color = "#ADD8E6"
        weight_color = "#FF69B4"
        gatekeeper_color = "#FF4500"
        output_color = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Inputs enter the network and travel from left to right.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(input_color)
        
        input_1 = Text("350", font_size=36, color=input_color)
        input_2 = Text("10", font_size=36, color=input_color)
        self.place_at_grid(input_1, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(input_2, "E1")
        
        label_1 = Text("Temp (°F)", font_size=18, color=input_color)
        label_2 = Text("Time (min)", font_size=18, color=input_color)
        label_1.next_to(input_1, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_2.next_to(input_2, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(input_1, label_1), FadeIn(input_2, label_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Each input is multiplied by a weight.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(weight_color)
        
        gatekeeper = Circle(radius=0.5, color=gatekeeper_color, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(gatekeeper, "C4")
        gatekeeper_label = Text("Gatekeeper", font_size=20, color=gatekeeper_color)
        gatekeeper_label.next_to(gatekeeper, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        line_1 = Line(input_1.get_right(), gatekeeper.get_left(), color=weight_color)
        line_2 = Line(input_2.get_right(), gatekeeper.get_left(), color=weight_color)
        
        weight_label_1 = Text("x Weight A", font_size=16, color=weight_color)
        weight_label_2 = Text("x Weight B", font_size=16, color=weight_color)
        
        # Placing labels between inputs and the gatekeeper
        self.place_at_grid(weight_label_1, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_label_2, "E3")
        weight_label_1.shift(DOWN * 0.2)
        weight_label_2.shift(UP * 0.2)

        self.play(Create(line_1), Create(line_2))
        self.play(FadeIn(weight_label_1), FadeIn(weight_label_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Weighted values are summed at each neuron.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(gatekeeper_color)
        
        dot_1 = Dot(input_1.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        dot_2 = Dot(input_2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(
            dot_1.animate.move_to(gatekeeper.get_center()),
            dot_2.animate.move_to(gatekeeper.get_center()),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.remove(dot_1, dot_2)
        
        sum_label = Text("+", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_label, "C4")
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # An activation function acts as a gatekeeper for signals.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(gatekeeper_color)
        
        self.remove(sum_label)
        self.play(FadeIn(gatekeeper), FadeIn(gatekeeper_label))
        # Pulse animation
        self.play(gatekeeper.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(gatekeeper.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_color(gatekeeper_color), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The final output is the network's current prediction.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(output_color)
        
        prediction = Text("Burnt Cookie", font_size=28, color=output_color)
        self.place_at_grid(prediction, "C6")
        
        arrow_out = Arrow(gatekeeper.get_right(), prediction.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow_out))
        self.play(FadeIn(prediction))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Iteration: Practice Makes Perfect
outline.content: Summarize that one step isn't enough. Learning is a cycle: Forward pass, calculate error, backpropagate blame, update dials, and repeat thousands of times until the error is near zero.
outline.example: The Robot Chef bakes 1,000 batches. Each time, it nudges the dials slightly based on the previous error, eventually discovering the 'Golden Recipe'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Iteration: Practice Makes Perfect",
            [
                "Learning requires repeating this cycle thousands of times.",
                "Each pass nudges the weights closer to perfection.",
                "Practice eventually transforms a random guess into accuracy."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        color_cycle = "#00BFFF"
        color_highlight = "#FFD700"
        
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_cycle))

        # Create cycle components
        forward_text = Text("Forward", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        loss_text = Text("Loss", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        backprop_text = Text("Backprop", font_size=20, color=WHITE)

        self.place_at_grid(forward_text, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(loss_text, "A5")
        self.place_in_area(backprop_text, "C3", "C4")

        cycle_group = VGroup(forward_text, loss_text, backprop_text)
        
        # Simple center for rotation (approximate)
        center_pos = (self.grid["B3"] + self.grid["B4"]) / 2
        
        # Circular Arrow Representation
        circle_path = Circle(radius=1.5, color=color_cycle).move_to(center_pos)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cycle_group), Create(circle_path))
        self.play(Rotate(circle_path, angle=TAU, about_point=center_pos), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_highlight)
        )

        # Create Graph for Error
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1, 0.2],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "D1", "F6")
        
        axes_label = Text("Error", font_size=18, color=WHITE).next_to(axes.y_axis, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Decreasing error curve
        error_curve = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 0.8 * np.exp(-0.5 * x),
            color=color_highlight,
            x_range=[0, 10]
        )

        self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_label))
        self.play(Create(error_curve), run_time=4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # "Golden Recipe" appears
        golden_recipe = Text("Golden Recipe", font_size=36, color=color_highlight)
        self.place_in_area(golden_recipe, "B2", "C5")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(cycle_group), 
            FadeOut(circle_path),
            FadeIn(golden_recipe)
        )
        
        self.play(Indicate(golden_recipe, color=color_highlight))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Loss Function: Measuring the Mistake", [
            "To improve, we must measure how wrong we are.",
            "The loss function calculates the distance from the truth.",
            "High loss means a large error in the prediction."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Prediction' (#FF0000) and 'Target' (#00FF00) as two distinct points on a vertical scale.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # Vertical Scale (Line from A3 to F3)
        scale_line = Line(self.grid["A3"], self.grid["F3"], color=GRAY_B)
        
        prediction_dot = Dot(color="#FF0000").scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(prediction_dot, "D3")
        prediction_label = Text("Prediction", font_size=20, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(prediction_label, "D4")
        
        target_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00").scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(target_dot, "B3")
        target_label = Text("Target", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(target_label, "B4")
        
        self.play(Create(scale_line))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(prediction_dot), Write(prediction_label),
            FadeIn(target_dot), Write(target_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a double-headed arrow (#FFFFE0) between the two points and label it 'Distance'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFE0")
        
        distance_arrow = DoubleArrow(
            prediction_dot.get_center(), 
            target_dot.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFFE0", 
            buff=0.1,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        distance_label = Text("Distance", font_size=22, color="#FFFFE0")
        self.place_at_grid(distance_label, "C4")
        
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(distance_arrow), Write(distance_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the formula 'Error = Prediction - Target' in #FFFFFF at the top of the screen.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\text{Error} = \text{Prediction} - \text{Target}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # We use updaters to ensure elements follow the prediction dot during the 'High loss' demonstration
        prediction_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(prediction_dot.get_center() + RIGHT * 1.0))
        distance_arrow.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(DoubleArrow(
            prediction_dot.get_center(), 
            target_dot.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFFE0", 
            buff=0.1,
            stroke_width=4
        )))
        distance_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to((prediction_dot.get_center() + target_dot.get_center())/2 + RIGHT * 1.0))

        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Increase distance to demonstrate "High loss"
        self.play(
            prediction_dot.animate.move_to(self.grid["F3"]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        prediction_label.clear_updaters()
        distance_arrow.clear_updaters()
        distance_label.clear_updaters()

outline.title: The Big Picture: Learning as Fine-Tuning
outline.content: Introduce the concept of a neural network as a series of adjustable 'dials' (weights). Explain that 'learning' is simply the process of turning these dials to get the correct output for a given input. Establish the prerequisite: inputs are numbers, and weights are multipliers.
outline.example: Imagine a Robot Chef trying to bake the perfect cookie. The 'inputs' are flour and sugar amounts; the 'dials' are how long it bakes and at what temperature.

storyboard.title: The Big Picture: Learning as Fine-Tuning
lecture_lines: Neural networks learn by adjusting internal parameters called weights.
Think of weights as dials on a machine.
Tuning these dials helps the network produce correct outputs.
animations: Create a simple neural network diagram with nodes on left (inputs) connected to a node on right (output). Label connections 'Weights' in #FFFFFF.
Animate 'Flour' and 'Sugar' icons (#FFD700) entering the input nodes from the left.
Show a rotating dial icon (#00FF00) over the connection lines to symbolize adjustment.
Scale the 'Weights' text labels while the dial icon rotates to indicate changing values.
Transform a 'Burnt Cookie' icon (#8B4513) at the output into a 'Perfect Cookie' (#F5DEB3).

        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Big Picture: Learning as Fine-Tuning"
        lines = [
            "Neural networks learn by adjusting internal parameters called weights.",
            "Think of weights as dials on a machine.",
            "Tuning these dials helps the network produce correct outputs."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Neural networks learn by adjusting internal parameters called weights.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Nodes
        input_node1 = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE)
        input_node2 = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE)
        output_node = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(input_node1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(input_node2, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(output_node, "C5")
        
        # Connections
        line1 = Line(input_node1.get_right(), output_node.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        line2 = Line(input_node2.get_right(), output_node.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        
        # Weights Label
        weights_label = Text("Weights", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(weights_label, "B3", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(input_node1), Create(input_node2), Create(output_node))
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.play(Write(weights_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Think of weights as dials on a machine.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        
        # Flour and Sugar icons entering
        flour_label = Text("Flour", font_size=16, color="#FFD700")
        sugar_label = Text("Sugar", font_size=16, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Using simple shapes for icons as no external assets provided
        flour_icon = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.4, color="#FFD700"), flour_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        sugar_icon = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.4, color="#FFD700"), sugar_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(flour_icon, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(sugar_icon, "D1")
        
        # Dial icon
        dial_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00FF00")
        dial_pointer = Line(dial_circle.get_center(), dial_circle.get_top(), color="#00FF00")
        dial = VGroup(dial_circle, dial_pointer)
        self.place_at_grid(dial, "C4")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(flour_icon, shift=RIGHT),
            FadeIn(sugar_icon, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        self.play(Create(dial))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Tuning these dials helps the network produce correct outputs.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Burnt Cookie at output
        burnt_label = Text("Burnt", font_size=16, color="#8B4513")
        burnt_cookie = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.3, color="#8B4513", fill_opacity=0.8), burnt_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(burnt_cookie, "C6")
        
        # Perfect Cookie
        perfect_label = Text("Perfect", font_size=16, color="#F5DEB3")
        perfect_cookie = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.3, color="#F5DEB3", fill_opacity=0.8), perfect_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(perfect_cookie, "C6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(burnt_cookie))
        
        # Rotate dial and scale weights
        self.play(
            Rotate(dial, angle=PI/2),
            weights_label.animate.scale(1.2),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Transform cookie
        self.play(Transform(burnt_cookie, perfect_cookie))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Gradient Descent: Walking Down the Hill
outline.content: Introduce the visual of a 'Loss Landscape' (a hilly terrain). Explain that the 'Gradient' tells us the direction of the steepest uphill. To learn, we take a small step in the opposite direction (downhill) to minimize error.
outline.example: The Robot Chef is in a foggy valley. It feels the slope under its feet and takes one small step toward the lowest point (the recipe with the least error).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The loss landscape is like a hilly, foggy terrain.",
            "The gradient points in the steepest uphill direction.",
            "We take a small step in the opposite direction.",
            "This process iteratively moves the network toward minimum error.",
            "Walking downhill reduces the overall cost of our model."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Gradient Descent: Walking Down the Hill", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a smooth U-shaped curve in #FFFFFF representing the 'Loss Landscape'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * (x**2), x_range=[-2.2, 2.2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        curve_center = curve.get_center()
        
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The gradient points in the steepest uphill direction.
        # Place a small 'Robot Chef' dot (#FFD700) at a high position on the slope.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        local_x_start = -1.6
        local_y_start = 0.5 * (local_x_start**2)
        dot = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.1)
        dot.move_to(curve_center + np.array([local_x_start, local_y_start, 0]))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        # Gradient arrow (uphill)
        uphill_arrow = Arrow(
            start=dot.get_center(), 
            end=dot.get_center() + np.array([-0.6, 0.9, 0]), 
            color="#00FF00", 
            buff=0
        )
        grad_label = Text("Gradient", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        grad_label.next_to(uphill_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(uphill_arrow), FadeIn(grad_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # We take a small step in the opposite direction.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Step arrow (downhill) - opposite of gradient
        downhill_arrow = Arrow(
            start=dot.get_center(), 
            end=dot.get_center() + np.array([0.6, -0.9, 0]), 
            color="#00FF00", 
            buff=0
        )
        step_label = Text("Step Down", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        step_label.next_to(downhill_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(uphill_arrow, downhill_arrow),
            ReplacementTransform(grad_label, step_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This process iteratively moves the network toward minimum error.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move dot one small 'step' down
        local_x_step = -0.8
        local_y_step = 0.5 * (local_x_step**2)
        step_pos = curve_center + np.array([local_x_step, local_y_step, 0])
        
        self.play(
            dot.animate.move_to(step_pos),
            FadeOut(downhill_arrow),
            FadeOut(step_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Iteratively move to the bottom
        bottom_pos = curve_center + np.array([0, 0, 0])
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(bottom_pos), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Walking downhill reduces the overall cost of our model.
        # Fade in the text 'Minimum Error' in #00FF00 at the lowest point of the curve.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        min_error_text = Text("Minimum Error", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        min_error_text.next_to(dot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(min_error_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Backpropagation: The Blame Game
outline.content: This is the core concept. Work backward from the error to see which 'dial' (weight) contributed most to the mistake. Explain that backpropagation is the application of the 'Chain Rule'—calculating the sensitivity of the final error to each individual weight.
outline.example: We look at the burnt cookie and ask: 'Was it mostly the temperature dial or the timer dial that caused this?' If the timer was off by 5 minutes but the temp only by 2 degrees, the timer gets more 'blame'.

storyboard.title: Backpropagation: The Blame Game
lecture_lines: Backpropagation traces the error back through the network.
We calculate how much each weight contributed to error.
The chain rule helps calculate these sensitivities precisely.
This assigns "blame" to specific dials in the system.
We now know which direction to turn each dial.
animations: Highlight the 'Error Score' in #FF0000 with a flashing effect to draw attention.
Animate arrows moving backward from the Error towards the Weights to show the flow of blame.
Color the 'Timer Weight' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/timer.svg] dark red (#8B0000) and 'Temp Weight' light red (#FA8072) based on contribution.
Display the mathematical symbol for the gradient 'dError/dWeight' in #00FFFF near the weights.
Highlight the weight [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dial.svg] with the highest error contribution using a glowing #FFFFFF border.

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Loss Function: Measuring the Mistake", [
            "To improve, we must measure how wrong we are.",
            "The loss function calculates the distance from the truth.",
            "High loss means a large error in the prediction."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Prediction' (#FF0000) and 'Target' (#00FF00) as two distinct points on a vertical scale.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # Vertical Scale (Line from A3 to F3)
        scale_line = Line(self.grid["A3"], self.grid["F3"], color=GRAY_B)
        
        prediction_dot = Dot(color="#FF0000").scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(prediction_dot, "D3")
        prediction_label = Text("Prediction", font_size=20, color="#FF0000")
        # Issue 27 fix: Adjusted scale_factor to 0.8 to prevent vertical crowding.
        self.place_at_grid(prediction_label, "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        target_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00").scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(target_dot, "B3")
        target_label = Text("Target", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        # Issue 27 fix: Adjusted scale_factor to 0.8 to prevent vertical crowding.
        self.place_at_grid(target_label, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(scale_line))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(prediction_dot), Write(prediction_label),
            FadeIn(target_dot), Write(target_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a double-headed arrow (#FFFFE0) between the two points and label it 'Distance'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFE0")
        
        distance_arrow = DoubleArrow(
            prediction_dot.get_center(), 
            target_dot.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFFE0", 
            buff=0.1,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        distance_label = Text("Distance", font_size=22, color="#FFFFE0")
        # Issue 27 fix: Adjusted scale_factor to 0.8 to prevent vertical crowding.
        self.place_at_grid(distance_label, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(distance_arrow), Write(distance_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the formula 'Error = Prediction - Target' in #FFFFFF at the top of the screen.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\text{Error} = \text{Prediction} - \text{Target}", color=WHITE)
        # Issue 26 fix: Adjusted scale_factor to 0.8 for better margins.
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # We use updaters to ensure elements follow the prediction dot during the 'High loss' demonstration
        # Position labels 1 grid unit to the right of the vertical scale
        prediction_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(prediction_dot.get_center() + RIGHT * 1.0))
        
        distance_arrow.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(DoubleArrow(
            prediction_dot.get_center(), 
            target_dot.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFFE0", 
            buff=0.1,
            stroke_width=4
        )))
        distance_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to((prediction_dot.get_center() + target_dot.get_center())/2 + RIGHT * 1.0))

        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Increase distance to demonstrate "High loss"
        self.play(
            prediction_dot.animate.move_to(self.grid["F3"]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        prediction_label.clear_updaters()
        distance_arrow.clear_updaters()
        distance_label.clear_updaters()
